.2. ¬(P ∧ Q)

message.content:
Looking at the premises:

1. (P ∧ Q)
2. ¬(P ∧ Q)

Premise 1 asserts that both P and Q are true simultaneously.
Premise 2 asserts that it is NOT the case that both P and Q are true simultaneously.

These two premises are direct contradictions of each other. Combining them yields:

(P ∧ Q) ∧ ¬(P ∧ Q)

This is a logical contradiction (always false). In classical propositional logic, a contradiction means the premises are inconsistent.

<answer>(P ∧ Q) ∧ ¬(P ∧ Q)</answer>
